summary: AstroCare is a health monitoring and early warning system designed to track astronauts' health conditions and identify potential health problems during space missions. The project monitors health indicators such as heart rate, body temperature, cabin CO₂ level, blood pressure, blood glucose and sleep duration etc. It aims to compare collected data with each astronaut's personal health history to detect unusual changes. AstroCare aims to support continuous health monitoring, identify potential risks at an early stage, and help medical teams make more informed decisions during space missions.
details: AstroCare is a health monitoring and support software designed to operate offline, enabling astronauts to independently track and manage their health status during long-duration space missions. The primary objective of our project is to facilitate the early detection of potential health issues, provide support to astronauts during emergencies, and help prevent minor health concerns from escalating into more serious complications. The software consists of five main modules: Daily Health Check-In, Symptom Guide, Weekly-Monthly Health Report, Exercise and Nutrition Plan, and Emergency. The Daily Health Check-In module performs daily health assessments by analyzing health data entered manually by astronauts, as well as information captured via cameras installed within their living quarters. The system is designed to utilize technologies similar to the ARCHeR system employed in Artemis missions; it compares astronauts' health metrics against established reference ranges to identify any deviations. Additionally, it provides questionnaire-based assessments to monitor the astronauts' mental well-being and identify potential psychological issues. The Symptom Guide module allows astronauts to indicate areas where they are experiencing pain or discomfort by selecting them on a digital model of the human body. Based on the selected body part and the reported symptoms, the software offers general information, advice, and recommendations to help astronauts manage their discomfort. This feature is intended solely for informational and support purposes; it does not provide medically valid diagnoses and is not a substitute for professional medical evaluation. Weekly-Monthly Health Report: This section analyzes health data collected from astronauts and presents changes in physical and mental health indicators through weekly and monthly reports. By identifying deviations from standard reference ranges and tracking changes over time, it provides recommendations on matters such as appropriate physical activities and nutritional choices. The system also enables the transmission of health reports to the mission control center on Earth whenever communication is possible. Based on the collected data and the generated recommendations, the astronauts' exercise and nutrition programs can be updated to reflect their evolving needs. Exercise and Nutrition Plan: This section provides astronauts with their daily exercise and nutrition regimens in a checklist format, making them easy to follow. It also includes activities that promote mental relaxation, such as breathing exercises and journaling. By evaluating the astronauts' daily routines and activity levels, AstroCare offers suggestions to help them refine their programs, maintain healthy habits, and support their overall physical and psychological well-being. Emergency: The Emergency section is designed to detect potentially critical health situations using cameras installed in the astronauts' living quarters and compatible monitoring technologies, such as ARCHeR. In the event of a detected emergency, the system uses voice commands to assess the astronaut's consciousness and responsiveness, while providing relevant emergency guidance. It is also designed to alert the mission control center on Earth and other crew members. Through voice instructions, the software guides the crew on the appropriate emergency response procedures. Once the emergency has concluded, the system can offer improvement recommendations aimed at reducing the likelihood of similar incidents recurring. Thanks to its simple and user-friendly interface, AstroCare enables astronauts to input and review their daily health data with minimal effort. Its offline functionality is particularly significant for long-duration space missions, where communication delays or temporary loss of connectivity with Earth could otherwise limit access to external medical support. By integrating daily health tracking, a symptom guide, health reports, personalized exercise and nutrition plans, and emergency support into a single platform, AstroCare aims to enhance the autonomy of astronauts in managing their own health. Through personalized recommendations, we strive to help astronauts maintain their physical and psychological well-being, sustain their performance, and carry out their daily tasks more efficiently. Our project was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Visual Studio Code.
